description.narrative: Improve the quality of secondary education, with a focus on underserved areas.

The objective of the Second Secondary Education Development Program Project (SEDP II) for Tanzania is to improve the quality of secondary education with a focus on underserved areas. There are four components to the project. The first component of the project is upgrading existing schools infrastructure. The objective of this component is to increase the number of secondary schools meeting minimum infrastructure requirements, moving them toward becoming fully functional per SEDP II. The component will provide support for rehabilitation and completion of existing school structures, with a minimum cost-effective infrastructure package. The second component of the project is improving the equitable provision of teachers and the quality of teaching in mathematics, sciences, and languages. The objectives of this component are deployment of teachers to rural areas; improved instruction in mathematics, sciences (biology, chemistry, and physics), and languages; and better teaching practices. The third component of the project is ensuring adequate financing to secondary schools and improving utilization of resources. The objective of this component is to ensure that adequate financing is provided to public secondary schools for the purchase of teaching and learning materials (currently at Tsh. 25,000 per student), and that these resources are disbursed timely and monitored effectively. The fourth and final component of the project is providing capacity building and technical assistance to implement reforms. The objective of this component is to strengthen institutional capacity for educational management. Sustained inputs to strengthen capacity for planning, management, delivery, and monitoring and supervision of education are critical to improving the quality and efficiency of education service delivery.

comment.narrative: The Government secured 2.5m million Mathematics and Science textbook in 2015. Additional 2.0 million are being printed by TIE under single textbook policy using Government budget. The project is contributing part of the large program and therefore there was no specific allocation from the project.

title.narrative: Improved examination pass rates in mathematics, sciences, and languages

target.value: O-level: Mathematics: 21% Sciences: 54% Languages: 69% A-level: Mathematics: 83% Sciences: 80% Languages: 96%

comment.narrative: Same values as reported in the last ISR are maintained. End target figures in the previous ISR was incorrect. Despite fall in pass rate for O Level Mathematics, pass rate for Sciences and Languages are above the target.

A cumulative total of 2193 classrooms (phase 1&2) have been added from SEDPII operation against the target of 4800. However, data from school report for 2016 indicated that 8790 classrooms were construed from 2010 to 2016 under community support as part of SEDPII program but are not reported. Therefore, when the Government input is taken into account, target is surpassed
Over all a total of 34,20 teachers were trained.  The project benefitted from resources from other Bank operations and other donors.

The indicator performance is above the target. The positive performance is attributed by improved enrolment as a result of implementation of free basic education and more students joining higher secondary education following a successful improvement passing (in division I-III) in end of lower secondary examinations and hence qualify to enroll in form five.
Enrolment for girls is above the target. This is attributed by improved school environment and successful community sensitization program. Despite the achievement, the overall quality of girl’s performance in examination is still low.

comment.narrative: The indicator performance is above the target for two main reasons. Improved school teaching and learning environment such as school infrastructure (teacher houses in hard to reach schools, classrooms, toiles for teaches and water) creating conducive environment for teacher retention 2011 Despite this positive achievement, the system is experiencing a huge shortage of Mathematics and science teachers. Figure for actual (previous) is incorrect generated by the system, the correct figure recorded in the last ISR was 20.

title.narrative: Student-qualified teacher ratio (SQTR) for 500 hard to reach schools

comment.narrative: The indicator has slightly declined by from 1:19 to 1:20. This is due to data cleaning as part of 2016 data collection finalized in August 2016. However, the performance is still above the target for two main reasons. Improved school teaching and learning envionment such as school infrastructure (classrooms, toiles for teaches and water) creating conducive environment for teacher retention A second reason is the growing number of teachers being trained in teacher programs, which has expanded the supply of qualified teachers. The project contribution includes provision of laboratory and chemicals to 7 mathematics and science teacher training colleges (with 4200 teaching capacity), supporting special diploma for mathematics and science program.  Despite this positive achievement, the system is experiencing a huge shortage of Mathematics and science teachers.

comment.narrative: The actual completion rate observed for the country in 2016 is considerably higher, equal to 5.4%. This is partly contributed by increased number of students passing form 4 at division I-III and joining higher secondary education.

comment.narrative: Same values as reported in the last ISR are maintained. Results for 2016 will not be available. The actual completion rate reached 33.6% at the O-level (Form 4) in Tanzania during 2015, above its revised new target. This is contributed by increased enrolment in community government schools, and improved student retention as a result of school leadership- and in-service teacher training programs
